patent: Fibre metal laminate: thin metal sheets bonded with a glass-filament prepreg, using a high-modulus SiO_{2}-Al_{2}O_{3}-MgO glass (S2-glass in the examples) in place of E-glass. Filed 1988-10-11 on a Netherlands priority of 1987-10-14. Test laminates, coded ALGLA, pair 2024-T3 sheets with a glass/epoxy prepreg; S2 and E versions are compared for notch strength, residual strength and fatigue crack growth. Claim 10 covers an aircraft fuselage with a skin sheet of the laminate. Possible link to GLARE, not confirmed: TU Delft states that Akzo Nobel filed the patent for GLARE in 1987 and that GLARE is applied on the Airbus A380. The assignee (Akzo) and priority date match, but that page does not name this number and no source checked does.

figs.1: Tensile nett strength against stress concentration factor. Solid ALGLA 2S (described as ALGLA-2S42) has three test points at K_{t} 1,0, 2,08 and 3,18; the callouts name the coupon for each point. Dashed ALGLA 2E42 is the E-glass laminate, crossing below 7075-T6 near K_{t} 2,2. The ordinate is broken below 400 MPa, so it does not start at zero.

figs.2: Tensile nett strength against total saw-cut length 2a, with tests at 10, 30 and 60 mm per the description. The abscissa prints no unit. ALGLA 2S32 stands furthest above ALGLA 2E32 at the shortest cut.
figs.2A: Residual-strength coupon, rectangular, with five holes in each end band. The small central circle is the only feature at the cut location; no slit is drawn.
figs.3: Half crack length a against thousands of cycles under sinusoidal loading at 10 Hz, with the load box inset. The bracket at lower left marks the starting half length; the description gives a total cut 2a = 3 mm. 2024-T3 rises steeply within the first 100 K cycles; both laminates grow almost linearly. The description assigns the plot to FIG. 3A and the coupon to FIG. 3, the reverse of the labels on the sheets.

figs.4A: Fatigue coupon for FIG. 4: drawn narrower than FIG. 3A, with three larger holes in each end band and a small central circle at the cut location.

glossary.def: Metal sheets bonded with fibre-reinforced resin layers; a crack in the metal is bridged by the intact fibres.
A commercial fibre metal laminate family of aluminium sheets and glass-fibre prepreg. See the patent note for the status of the link to this patent.
Tensile strength with a hole or slot present, as defined at col. 2. Related modern test: open-hole tension.
K_{t}: peak stress at a notch divided by nominal stress on the remaining section.
Failure load divided by the remaining cross-section at the notch.
Tensile strength remaining with a crack or saw-cut present.
Fatigue stress ratio, minimum stress over maximum stress. R = 0 is tension from zero, as in a pressure cabin cycle.
Reinforcing filaments already impregnated with uncured resin, cured in place by heat and pressure.

Reinforcement glasses. The patent gives E-glass at about 55% SiO_{2} with CaO and B_{2}O_{3}, and its own filaments at 58–69% SiO_{2}, 18–29% Al_{2}O_{3}, 7–19% MgO. S2 is the Owens Corning Fiberglas trademark named at col. 4.
Aluminium-copper and aluminium-zinc alloys; T3 and T6 are heat-treatment temper codes.
Test laminates. Per the description, S or E is the glass type, and 42 or 32 goes with 0,4 or 0,3 mm aluminium sheets. The patent does not spell out the code.
The description writes most decimals with a comma (0,35 GPa); the claims use a point.
